title: Schur–Zassenhaus and the Splitting of Normal Sylow Subgroups
description: Answers the parent Sylow entry's open question by formalizing the Schur–Zassenhaus splitting theorem (a normal subgroup of coprime order and index has a complement) and deriving the Sylow extension it asks for: a normal Sylow p-subgroup is always complemented by a Hall p′-subgroup, so the group splits as an internal semidirect product G = P ⋊ K. Built on Mathlib's existence half of Schur–Zassenhaus, with the structural consequences (disjointness, generation, complement order = index) proved here.

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: Sylow's theorems. This entry answers its listed open question on formalizing Schur–Zassenhaus as an extension of Sylow theory.

overview.historicalContext:
The Schur–Zassenhaus theorem (Schur 1904 for the abelian kernel case, Zassenhaus 1937 in general) states that if `N` is a normal subgroup of a finite group `G` with `gcd(|N|, [G:N]) = 1`, then `N` has a complement `K` — a subgroup with `N ∩ K = 1` and `NK = G` — so that `G` is the internal semidirect product `N ⋊ K`. It is one of the cornerstones of finite group theory and the foundation of the theory of group extensions: it guarantees that an extension `1 → N → G → Q → 1` with coprime `|N|` and `|Q|` always splits.

The theorem connects directly to Sylow theory. A Sylow `p`-subgroup `P` of a finite group is a Hall subgroup: `|P|` is a power of `p` and `[G:P]` is coprime to `p`, hence `gcd(|P|, [G:P]) = 1` automatically. Therefore, whenever a Sylow subgroup happens to be normal, Schur–Zassenhaus immediately provides a complement — a `p`-complement, i.e. a Hall `p′`-subgroup. This is the precise sense in which Schur–Zassenhaus 'extends' Sylow theory, and is exactly the open question raised by the parent gallery entry.

Mathlib formalizes the existence half of Schur–Zassenhaus (`Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime`). This entry packages that result, proves the structural consequences (the complement's order, disjointness, and generation), and derives the Sylow corollary.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem as an extension of Sylow theory: (1) state that a normal subgroup `N` with `gcd(|N|, [G:N]) = 1` has a complement `K` realizing `G = N ⋊ K`; (2) record the structural data `N ⊓ K = ⊥`, `N ⊔ K = ⊤`, `|K| = [G:N]`; (3) derive that a normal Sylow `p`-subgroup is always complemented by a Hall `p′`-subgroup.
overview.proofStrategy: The existence of a complement is `Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime` from Mathlib's Schur–Zassenhaus development. From a complement pair `IsComplement' N K` we read off the structure: disjointness and generation come from the `IsCompl` packaged inside `IsComplement'`, and the complement's order `|K| = [G:N]` follows by cancelling `|N|` in `|N|·|K| = |G| = |N|·[G:N]` (Lagrange). For the Sylow corollary, `Sylow.card_coprime_index` supplies the coprimality hypothesis for free — a Sylow `p`-subgroup is a Hall subgroup — so a normal Sylow subgroup satisfies Schur–Zassenhaus with no further work, and `Sylow.not_dvd_index` shows the complement is a `p′`-group.
keyInsights: Schur–Zassenhaus is the splitting principle for coprime extensions: gcd(|N|, [G:N]) = 1 forces 1 → N → G → G/N → 1 to split, so G = N ⋊ K.
Sylow subgroups are Hall subgroups — |P| is a p-power and [G:P] is coprime to p — so the coprimality hypothesis of Schur–Zassenhaus is automatic for them. Normality is the only missing ingredient.
Hence a normal Sylow p-subgroup is always complemented, by a Hall p′-subgroup. This is the precise bridge from Sylow theory to the theory of group extensions that the parent entry asked for.
The complement's order is determined: |K| = [G:N], obtained purely from Lagrange's theorem |N|·[G:N] = |G| and the complement identity |N|·|K| = |G|.
Everything is stated for an arbitrary finite group via Nat.card, so it applies uniformly without choosing a presentation or a concrete group.

sections.title: Overview: from Sylow theory to group extensions

sections.title: Section I: Schur–Zassenhaus Existence and the Complement's Order
sections.summary: schurZassenhaus restates Mathlib's existence theorem (a coprime normal subgroup has a complement); isComplement'_card_eq_index proves |K| = [G:N] by cancelling |N| in |N|·|K| = |G| = |N|·[G:N].

sections.title: Section II: The Internal Semidirect Product
sections.summary: schurZassenhaus_structure bundles disjointness (N ⊓ K = ⊥), generation (N ⊔ K = ⊤), and the order |K| = [G:N] into the full semidirect-product statement; complement_of_coprime_orders gives the |G| = m·n factorization phrasing used in small-order classification.
sections.mathContext: A coprime normal subgroup splits off: G is the internal semidirect product N ⋊ K with K of order exactly [G:N].

sections.title: Section III: The Sylow Extension — Normal Sylow Subgroups Split
sections.summary: normalSylow_isComplemented: a normal Sylow p-subgroup is complemented (coprimality from Sylow.card_coprime_index). normalSylow_complement_card / _not_dvd / _coprime: the complement has order [G:P], is a Hall p′-subgroup (p ∤ |K|), and has order coprime to |P|.
sections.mathContext: When a Sylow subgroup is normal, the Hall property makes Schur–Zassenhaus apply automatically, yielding a p-complement and the splitting G = P ⋊ K.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) formalization, in 121 lines with 8 theorems, of the Schur–Zassenhaus splitting theorem and its Sylow corollary. The existence of a complement is invoked from Mathlib; the structural consequences (|K| = [G:N], N ⊓ K = ⊥, N ⊔ K = ⊤) and the Sylow extension (a normal Sylow p-subgroup is complemented by a Hall p′-subgroup) are proved here.
conclusion.implications: This answers the parent Sylow entry's open question, formalizing Schur–Zassenhaus precisely as an extension of Sylow theory: the Hall property of Sylow subgroups makes the coprimality hypothesis automatic, so normality of a Sylow p-subgroup alone forces an internal semidirect decomposition G = P ⋊ K. The order-factorization phrasing and the explicit complement order make the results directly usable as building blocks for small-order group classification (e.g. groups of order pq, p²q), where a normal Sylow subgroup repeatedly splits the group.
openQuestions: Formalize the conjugacy half of Schur–Zassenhaus: when N (or G/N) is solvable, all complements of N are conjugate. This is the harder direction and underpins the uniqueness in small-order classification.

Combine with the parent's Sylow counting to give a Lean decision procedure: for many n ≤ 100, a Sylow subgroup is forced normal, so Schur–Zassenhaus yields the full semidirect-product structure of every group of order n.

mainTheorems.name: schurZassenhaus
mainTheorems.description: Schur–Zassenhaus (existence): a normal subgroup N whose order is coprime to its index [G:N] has a complement K, so the multiplication N × K → G is a bijection.
mainTheorems.leanType: {N : Subgroup G} → [N.Normal] → (h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index) → ∃ K : Subgroup G, IsComplement' N K

mainTheorems.name: schurZassenhaus_structure
mainTheorems.description: Schur–Zassenhaus (structure): the complement K realizes an internal semidirect product G = N ⋊ K — N and K are disjoint (N ⊓ K = ⊥), generate G (N ⊔ K = ⊤), and |K| = [G:N].
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → {N : Subgroup G} → [N.Normal] → (h : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index) → ∃ K : Subgroup G, IsComplement' N K ∧ N ⊓ K = ⊥ ∧ N ⊔ K = ⊤ ∧ Nat.card K = N.index

mainTheorems.name: complement_of_coprime_orders
mainTheorems.description: Order-factorization phrasing: if |G| = m·n via a normal N of order m and index n with gcd(m,n)=1, then G has a subgroup of order n complementing N — the classical coprime-order splitting.
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → {N : Subgroup G} → [N.Normal] → {m n : ℕ} → (Nat.card N = m) → (N.index = n) → (Nat.Coprime m n) → ∃ K : Subgroup G, IsComplement' N K ∧ Nat.card K = n

mainTheorems.name: normalSylow_isComplemented
mainTheorems.description: Sylow extension of Schur–Zassenhaus: a NORMAL Sylow p-subgroup is always complemented. Sylow subgroups are Hall (card coprime to index), so coprimality is automatic and normality is the only extra hypothesis; the complement gives G = P ⋊ K.
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → [Fact p.Prime] → (P : Sylow p G) → [(P : Subgroup G).Normal] → ∃ K : Subgroup G, IsComplement' (P : Subgroup G) K

mainTheorems.name: isComplement'_card_eq_index
mainTheorems.description: The complement of a coprime normal subgroup has order equal to the index [G:N], by cancelling |N| in |N|·|K| = |G| = |N|·[G:N].
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → {N K : Subgroup G} → (h : IsComplement' N K) → Nat.card K = N.index

mainTheorems.name: normalSylow_complement_card
mainTheorems.description: The complement of a normal Sylow p-subgroup has order equal to the index [G:P].
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → [Fact p.Prime] → (P : Sylow p G) → [(P : Subgroup G).Normal] → {K : Subgroup G} → (IsComplement' (P : Subgroup G) K) → Nat.card K = (P : Subgroup G).index

mainTheorems.name: normalSylow_complement_not_dvd
mainTheorems.description: The complement of a normal Sylow p-subgroup is a Hall p′-subgroup: p does not divide its order, so normality of a Sylow subgroup forces a p-complement.
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → [Fact p.Prime] → (P : Sylow p G) → [(P : Subgroup G).Normal] → {K : Subgroup G} → (IsComplement' (P : Subgroup G) K) → ¬ p ∣ Nat.card K

mainTheorems.name: normalSylow_complement_coprime
mainTheorems.description: The complement's order is coprime to that of the Sylow subgroup — exactly the statement that G is the internal semidirect product of the two coprime Hall subgroups P and K.
mainTheorems.leanType: [Finite G] → [Fact p.Prime] → (P : Sylow p G) → [(P : Subgroup G).Normal] → {K : Subgroup G} → (IsComplement' (P : Subgroup G) K) → Nat.Coprime (Nat.card (P : Subgroup G)) (Nat.card K)
